messages.content:
Plan this as a Rhylthyme meal and deliver a live timeline: Three-Course Dinner for Six: Two Burners, One Oven for 6 people, three courses, following the source text below
Resource limits: one oven, two burners, one cook, courses go out in order.
Everything must be finished by 19:30.
Steps:
1. Check the public catalog first (search_public_recipes or cook_recipe). If a good match exists, use it and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise read rhylthyme://guide/authoring and build a program: one track per parallel line of work, sequential steps chained with afterStep, realistic durations, and a resourceConstraint for every task.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON. A machine that runs one job at a time is `resourceConstraints[].maxConcurrent`. Work repeated n times (n trays, n samples, n aircraft) is `replicates: {count: n, mode: "serial" | "parallel" | "stagger"}` on ONE step — never n hand-copied steps or tracks. Chain what follows each repetition with `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"<step>","instances":"each"}`, and give the step that waits for all of them `"instances":"all"`. When a holding area between them only fits k at a time (a rack that holds two trays, a rotor that holds six tubes, a taxiway that holds two aircraft), set `replicates.maxInFlight: k` so the upstream step is held back instead of stranding the downstream one.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule with finishAt="19:30" to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.

Source text to schedule (read all of it):
<<<
Three-Course Dinner for Six: Two Burners, One Oven

Guests sit down at half past seven. There are two burners, one oven and one cook, so the oven does the braise first and the tart second, and the burners are rarely both free.

Mise en place
Chop the mirepoix, trim the short ribs and measure the stock: forty minutes of knife work before anything goes on the heat.

Main: braised short ribs
Heat the oven to 300°F; give it 20 minutes. Sear the short ribs in a heavy pot over high heat for 12 minutes, turning once. Lift the ribs out, soften the mirepoix in the same pot for 8 minutes, add the wine and reduce it for 5 minutes, then return the ribs with the stock. Braise the ribs, covered, for 3 hours. Rest the pot off the heat for 20 minutes, then skim the fat and reduce the braising liquid for 15 minutes.

Starter: leek and potato soup
Two hours into the braise, sweat the sliced leeks in butter for 10 minutes. Add the potatoes and the stock and simmer for 30 minutes, then blend the soup smooth; 5 minutes. Hold it warm on the back burner until the guests are seated.

Dessert: apple tart
Roll the pastry and line the tin; 15 minutes. Chill the shell in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes and no more than two hours. Slice the apples and arrange them in the shell; 20 minutes. Bake the tart for 45 minutes the moment the ribs leave the oven, while the ribs are resting.

Service
Ladle the soup when everyone is seated; ten minutes at the table. Plate the ribs ten minutes after the soup bowls are cleared, and give the plating five minutes. Let the main course run as long as it runs. The tart goes out twenty minutes after the main plates come back; ten minutes to slice and serve.
>>>

validate_program reported 1 error(s):

Fix every error and reply with the complete corrected program JSON in a single ```json fenced block.
